summary: Terminal stream shows the shell commands an agent runs as a compact terminal panel. The header has the working directory and how the run is going, with Stop while it runs and Copy. Each command shows as a `$ npm run build` line with its output streaming in underneath, and ends with a check or a red exit code, and how long it took. Output longer than five lines folds to its last four behind a "Show 24 more lines" button, and when the run is over a line at the foot sums it up, like "Ran 3 commands".
use: When an agent installs, builds and tests code, and people want to see what it ran and what came back.
When a command fails and people need the failing lines, the agent's reading of them and the fix in one place.
When long output like a build log should be there if wanted, without filling the panel.
When people need a way to stop a run that is going wrong, or to copy the whole run into an issue or a chat.
features: `entries` are commands, notes and edits, oldest first. A command has a `status` of `running`, `ok`, `failed` or `stopped`, with a spinner, a green check, a red "Exit 1" tag (from `exitCode`) or a Stopped tag, and its `duration`. A grey line runs down its left, in the accent and pulsing while it runs and red if it failed; Clean leaves the line out.
Output lines can be coloured with a `tone`: `ok` green, `bad` red or `muted` grey. Lines wrap inside the panel, so a long line never scrolls the page sideways.
Output longer than `tail` + 1 lines folds to its last `tail` lines (4 by default) behind a "Show N more lines" button that opens the rest.

A note (`kind: 'note'`) is a line from the agent between commands, which shimmers while it is the newest entry of a run still going. An edit (`kind: 'edit'`) is a file it changed, with a pencil in place of the `$`, the lines added and removed once it is done, and its `diff` under it: lines starting with "-" on a red tint and "+" on a green one.

The header shows `cwd` and the run's `status` as a tag: grey while it runs, with `elapsed` beside Running shimmering like every loading line, then green when passed or red when failed. In Blueprint and Soft a light sweeps along the header's edge while it runs; in Clean the header is an off-white strip. `onStop` adds a Stop button while it runs, and Copy copies the whole run as text, edits' diffs included.

While the run goes on, a block cursor blinks after the newest line. The commands, their output and the diffs are code, in mono; the header, the times, the notes and the summary are in the interface's type.

Once the run is over, `summary` folds open at the foot. By default it says how many commands ran, counting each one once however many times it ran; how the run went is the header's tag, and the finished line has no clock.

Each command, note, edit and output line opens its own height as it arrives, with its words fading in, and the terminal grows with them in one continuous motion, up to 420px; then its output scrolls inside it and stays on the newest line, unless someone has scrolled up to read. In browsers that can't ease to an auto height, lines arrive at once and the terminal eases to them. To change the most it grows to, give it a `className` and set `max-height` on it and on its `.dm-grow` child in your CSS.
a11y: The output is a log region labelled "Terminal output", so screen readers can follow it as it arrives. It can be focused with Tab and scrolled with the arrow keys.
"Show N more lines" is a button that says whether the folded lines are open, and the folded lines can't be reached with Tab while they are shut.

Stop and Copy are labelled buttons, and Copy says "Copied to clipboard" in a tooltip once it has copied, its icon crossfading into a tick. A command's spinner, and the header's, crossfade the same way into the tick, Exit tag or Stopped that ends them.
The coloured lines, the sweeping light, the shimmer and the cursor are decoration: each command's state is also written out, and with reduced motion they stop moving.

faq.a: No. It shows the `entries` you pass. Your code runs the commands, streams their output into `output`, and sets each one's `status` and `duration`. `onStop` tells you when someone pressed Stop.

faq.q: Why does the summary say Ran 3 commands when 4 ran?
faq.a: It counts each command once, however many times it ran, so a test run again after a fix doesn't add one. Pass your own `summary` to say it another way, or `false` to hide it.

faq.q: Can it show colours from the shell?
faq.a: Not ANSI codes. Give each line a `tone` instead: `ok`, `bad` or `muted`.
